title: Lifting a computation to a larger tape bank
statement: Let $M$ and $B$ be finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machines with $M$ using a positive number of work tapes and no more work tapes than $B$. Let $e$ map the states of $M$ to states of $B$, and suppose that for every source state and every input/work-tape scan, $B$'s transition at the embedded state is the padded action of $M$'s transition, reading $M$'s work tapes from the corresponding initial block. If $M$, started in state $q$ on input $x$ with word $s$ on its first work tape and all remaining tapes blank, is halted at time $T$ with output $y$, then $B$, started in state $e(q)$ on input $x$ with the same initial tape contents, is halted at time $T$ with output $y$.
